content_voiceover: This slide lays out the guideline recommended regimens for marginal zone lymphoma by treatment line. First line preferred options, listed alphabetically so no hierarchy is implied, are bendamustine plus rituximab, CHOP plus rituximab, and CVP plus rituximab. For low tumor burden nodal disease, single agent rituximab is reasonable. For older or infirm patients who wouldn't tolerate combination chemoimmunotherapy, the preferred approach is rituximab monotherapy or involved site radiotherapy alone. An optional extended therapy phase adds rituximab maintenance every eight to twelve weeks for up to two years. Second line and subsequent therapy preferred options include bendamustine rituximab if not previously used, covalent BTK inhibitors such as zanubrutinib after at least one prior anti CD20 based regimen, CHOP or CVP with rituximab, and lenalidomide plus rituximab. For frailer patients in the second line setting, covalent BTKi again leads, alongside lenalidomide rituximab and rituximab monotherapy. Third line and beyond now centers on CD19 directed CAR T cell therapy, specifically lisocabtagene maraleucel as preferred, with axicabtagene ciloleucel as another recommended option, and allogeneic transplant reserved for highly selected cases as consolidation.
keypoints: First line preferred: bendamustine rituximab, R-CHOP, or R-CVP
Older or infirm patients: rituximab monotherapy or radiotherapy alone
Second line preferred: BTK inhibitors, bendamustine rituximab, lenalidomide rituximab
Extended maintenance rituximab can follow first or second line therapy
Third line: CD19 directed CAR T cell therapy, especially liso-cel
keypoint_voiceover: For boards, anchor on three tiers: first line is BR, R-CHOP, or R-CVP, second line brings in BTK inhibitors and lenalidomide rituximab, and third line and beyond is CAR T cell therapy, with liso-cel preferred over axi-cel in this setting.
